display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#333333, #c1c1c1); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Estimates (assumptions)
• Write (create an order at a partner), 50 RPS, API responds in 20–30 s
• Little's law, synchronous: 50 × 25 s = 1,250 requests in flight — cannot hold user connections that long
Choice
Writes — queue and background processing (202 + status). Reads — cache + background refresh.
Cost: a queue, workers, operation statuses, eventual consistency, a "processing" UX.
Retries
• Timeout or 500 ≠ "not done" — retry only with the same Idempotency-Key
• No key — check the status by our reference id first
• Never retry 4xx — mark failed right away
Failure: API is down for an hour
• Circuit breaker opens, a probe request every 30 s
• The queue grows by 50 × 3,600 = 180,000 jobs, ~180 MB
• Bulkhead: a dedicated worker pool, the rest of the service keeps working
• After recovery — ramp up gradually within the API rate limit
What breaks first at ×10 (500 RPS)
1. The external API rate limit — negotiate, batch, cache
2. 12,500 concurrent calls: sockets, maxSockets, memory
3. An hour of downtime — 1.8M jobs, ~1.8 GB in Redis
